hero.title: The Tipitaka: Buddhist Canonical Texts
hero.description: The Tipitaka constitutes the foundational body of scripture in Pali for Theravada Buddhism, representing the earliest record of Buddha's teachings.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of the Canon from oral tradition to written form.

cards.details: First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha; Upali and Ananda recite Vinaya and Sutta.
Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali; initial signs of sectarian divisions.
Aluvihara Rock Temple (Sri Lanka); Tipitaka first committed to writing during the reign of Vattagamani Abhaya.

items: Commonly confused: Abhidhamma is not attributed directly to Buddha like the Suttas, but to later scholastic developments.
Tipitaka is written in Pali, not Sanskrit (Sanskrit texts belong to Mahayana Buddhism, e.g., Mahavastu).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Structure

  • Vinaya Pitaka: Conduct
  • Sutta Pitaka: Discourses
  • Abhidhamma Pitaka: Philosophy

Key Reciters

  • Ananda: Dhamma expert
  • Upali: Vinaya expert

Detailed Breakdown

  • Vinaya Pitaka (Basket of Discipline): Rules for monks/nuns. Subdivided into Sutta Vibhanga, Khandhaka, and Parivara.
  • Sutta Pitaka (Basket of Discourses): Collection of Buddha's teachings. Comprises 5 Nikayas (Digha, Majjhima, Samyutta, Anguttara, Khuddaka).
  • Abhidhamma Pitaka (Basket of Higher Teachings): Philosophical interpretation. Contains 7 texts including Dhammasangani.
